identity.name: agent
identity.description: Pi agent home under ~/.pi/agent: settings, extensions, skills, prompts, observability, and npm-installed agent packages — not a conventional application repo.

leadContext.note: Lead is session-rich; Pass A stays project/static and only cross-checks lead friction against on-disk harness structure.

gitignore.effect: Most harness config is ignored; only skills tree is whitelist-eligible. Three config files remain tracked from earlier force-add/commit and are not newly addable under current ignore rules without -f.

observability.shape: session-end token/cost metrics only; no structured diagnostic events, correlation ids, or failure taxonomy

gitStatusSummary.note: Packet 453 changed files dominated by untracked skills (incl. __pycache__); not a conventional app source delta.

dimensionScores.summary: Operational rules exist in APPEND_SYSTEM.md and ce-lite, but there is no versioned AGENTS/SYSTEM/README/DESIGN contract; skill allowlist contradicts APPEND_SYSTEM triggers.
Rich package/extension stack and deny-by-default gitignore, but no command surface, hooks, or CI; triggered specialist skills are filtered out of loading.
No package scripts, tests, pre-commit, or CI. Critical-severity working tree (453 files / 266k lines) has no validation gate.
Only 3 tracked files; harness-critical artifacts (APPEND_SYSTEM, inventory, agents, extensions code) are gitignored. Delivery and recovery surfaces are not versioned.
memory/, sessions/, observability/, and harness-inventory exist, but inventory is stale/untracked and history.jsonl is metric-only (4 lines).

findings.title: No durable agent instruction contract (AGENTS/SYSTEM/README/DESIGN)
evidence: packet projectProfile.agentInstructions.status=none, count=0
disk: no agent/AGENTS.md, agent/SYSTEM.md, agent/README.md, DESIGN.md
APPEND_SYSTEM.md exists and defines CE-lite + skill triggers, but is ignored by root gitignore '*'
findings.impact: Agents restart without a versioned project contract; packet recommendedReads cannot anchor on instruction files; onboarding and multi-agent consistency rely on ephemeral/local-only files.
findings.fixDirection: Add versioned agent/AGENTS.md (or SYSTEM.md) summarizing harness purpose, command surface, skill policy, and non-negotiables; whitelist it in .gitignore; keep APPEND_SYSTEM as thin overlay or merge into AGENTS.md.

findings.title: settings.skills allowlist blocks APPEND_SYSTEM trigger skills
evidence: settings.json skills: ["!**","**/ce-lite/**","**/better-harness/**"]
APPEND_SYSTEM.md triggers harness-doctor, poor-mans-distill, shard-security, context-rot-forensics, graph-engineering, workflow:codebase-audit
those skills exist under agent/skills/ (44 SKILL.md total) but do not match allowlist
better-harness SKILL.md only under npm/node_modules/@qoder-ai/better-harness/..., not under agent/skills/
findings.impact: User phrases that APPEND_SYSTEM maps to specialist skills will fail closed or silently no-op if the runtime honors the allowlist — controlled execution path is self-contradictory.
findings.fixDirection: Either expand skills allowlist to include every APPEND_SYSTEM trigger path, or remove/relocate those triggers; add a smoke check that each trigger resolves to a loadable SKILL.md.

findings.title: Root gitignore deny-all prevents versioning harness control plane
evidence: .gitignore: * then only !agent/skills/**
tracked files only: settings.json, context-prune/settings.json, extensions/pi-lean-ctx/config.json
check-ignore: APPEND_SYSTEM.md, harness-inventory.json, agents/Explore.md, extensions/transcript-pruner.ts all ignored by '*'
git status shows ?? agent/skills/ plus 3 modified tracked configs; porcelain ~469
findings.impact: Harness behavior is mostly non-reproducible across machines/clones; critical config and extension code cannot be reviewed or rolled back via git; packet under-reports real surface (0 sourceFiles) because ignore hides it.
findings.fixDirection: Replace blanket * with an explicit allowlist for harness control plane: settings.json, APPEND_SYSTEM.md/AGENTS.md, agents/**, extensions/**, hooks/**, prompts/**, workflows/**, observability/.gitignore policy, harness-inventory.json — while still ignoring sessions/, memory/blobs, npm/, caches, __pycache__.

findings.title: No validation command surface, hooks, or CI for harness changes
evidence: no agent/package.json, no root justfile/Makefile
no .github/workflows, no .pre-commit-config.yaml, no core.hooksPath / .githooks
packet followUpActions validate-impact only cites a fixture example under graph-engineering
diffImpact severity=critical score=100 on 453 files / 266023 lines with zero tests
findings.impact: Config and skill changes land without lint/load/smoke gates; skill __pycache__ and large trees enter the working tree unchecked.
findings.fixDirection: Add a minimal harness doctor/smoke entrypoint (e.g. scripts/harness-smoke.sh or npm script) that validates settings.json JSON, skills filter vs on-disk triggers, extension paths exist, and inventory freshness; wire pre-commit or a documented manual gate before commit.

findings.title: Observability and inventory are present but not operationalized
evidence: observability/history.jsonl has 4 lines of session-end usage metrics only
harness-inventory.json generated 2026-07-30T16:03:28+0100 (stale vs 2026-08-04 analysis)
inventory gitignored; no scheduled refresh command in versioned docs
lead session-rich mode shows weak durable learning capture — aligns with missing project-side learning artifacts
findings.impact: Cannot reconstruct failures, skill-load misses, or config drift from project artifacts; doctor/audit work lacks a fresh baseline.
findings.fixDirection: Define a small observability schema (event type, correlation id, skill id, outcome) beyond token totals; version inventory generation command and refresh policy; keep redacted inventory snapshot trackable.

findings.title: Working tree is a large untracked skills dump, not a scoped change
evidence: diffImpact reasons include wide file change count 453 and large changed-line count 266023
changeDrift sample dominated by untracked agent/skills/** including __pycache__ .pyc
history confidence low (3 commits / 6 days); only supporting hot files are the 3 tracked configs
coreAnalysis candidates=[] — no core boundary for this harness-home layout
findings.impact: Review and delivery cannot distinguish intentional skill installs from noise; critical severity is mostly inventory/untracked bulk, which can mask real config regressions in settings.json.
findings.fixDirection: Ignore **/__pycache__/** and *.pyc under skills; commit intentional skills in curated batches; treat settings.json / APPEND_SYSTEM / extensions as the true high-risk review set.

findings.title: Project profile is empty because git tracking ≠ actual harness surface
evidence: projectInfo.sourceFiles=0, languages=[], frameworks=[], manifests=[]
totals.trackedFiles=3 while disk has skills, extensions, prompts, workflows, npm packages
packet recommendedReads still points at the 3 tracked configs + untracked skills paths
findings.impact: Static pack understates architecture; agents following only tracked profile miss the real control plane.
findings.fixDirection: After gitignore allowlist fix, re-run project pack with path scope agent; optionally maintain a hand-written project overlay listing packages, extensions, and skill policy for better-harness.

findings.title: Local extension transcript-pruner.ts is runtime-critical but ignored
evidence: settings.json extensions includes ~/.pi/agent/extensions/transcript-pruner.ts
git check-ignore marks agent/extensions/transcript-pruner.ts ignored by '*'
only extensions/pi-lean-ctx/config.json is tracked under extensions/
findings.impact: Clone/restore loses transcript pruning behavior; settings will point at missing file.
findings.fixDirection: Track agent/extensions/*.ts (or the specific pruner) and add a startup existence check.

recommendations.title: Fix skills filter ↔ APPEND_SYSTEM trigger alignment
recommendations.action: Update settings.json skills allowlist to include every triggered skill path, or narrow APPEND_SYSTEM triggers to ce-lite/better-harness only until others are allowed.

recommendations.title: Version the harness control plane via gitignore allowlist
recommendations.action: Whitelist settings, instruction docs, agents/, extensions/, hooks/, prompts/, workflows/, and inventory; keep sessions/memory/npm/cache ignored.

recommendations.title: Add harness smoke/doctor command and document it in AGENTS.md
recommendations.action: Single entrypoint validating JSON configs, extension path existence, skill trigger resolution, inventory age; no full CI required initially.

recommendations.title: Reduce working-tree noise under skills
recommendations.action: gitignore __pycache__ and build artifacts; commit curated skills separately from experimental dumps.

recommendations.title: Operationalize observability + inventory refresh
recommendations.action: Refresh harness-inventory on a known cadence; extend history.jsonl beyond token totals for load/doctor/skill events.

softwareFluencyNarrative.taskUnderstanding: Weak formal contract; strong informal APPEND_SYSTEM/ce-lite voice. Skill policy and trigger table disagree.
softwareFluencyNarrative.controlledExecution: Extension/package ecosystem is sophisticated, but execution control lacks gates and the skill allowlist fails closed against documented triggers.
softwareFluencyNarrative.changeValidation: Essentially absent at repo level. Critical diff score is bulk untracked skills, not validated product change.
softwareFluencyNarrative.reliableDelivery: Deny-by-default gitignore protects secrets/noise but blocks delivering the harness itself. Three tracked config files are an incomplete delivery unit.
softwareFluencyNarrative.learningCapture: Directories exist (memory/sessions/observability/inventory) but content is thin/stale and not tied to a feedback loop.

Lead weak learning-capture facets match PH-A-005 thin observability/inventory.
Lead tool/skill routing complexity matches PH-A-002 allowlist vs triggers.
